back: The differences between individuals of the same species.
Variation giving a range of phenotypes between two extremes, with many intermediates.
notes: Examples: height, mass, leaf length, milk yield.

back: Variation giving a limited number of distinct phenotypes with no intermediates.
notes: Examples: ABO blood group, sex, tongue rolling, round or wrinkled peas.

back: Many genes together with the environment.
Usually genes only, often a single gene; the environment has little or no effect.
A histogram: equal class intervals, bars touching.
A bar chart with gaps between the bars.

front: Why can identical twins differ in mass?
back: They have the same genes, so differences come from the environment (diet, exercise, illness).

front: How to investigate variation in leaf length?
back: Measure a large random sample (30 or more), group into equal non-overlapping classes, draw a histogram, find the mean and range.

front: How do you calculate the **range** and the **mean**?
back: Range = largest value − smallest value. Mean = total of the values ÷ number of values.
